topicTitle: Advanced Pipes and Cisterns — Leak Scenarios

questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; with a leak it takes 7.5 hours. The leak empties a full tank in (hours)
An inlet delivers 12 litres per minute and a leak loses 2 litres per minute. A 600-litre tank fills in (minutes)
A leak empties a full tank in 20 hours. In 5 hours it empties what fraction of the tank?
A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours. The tank is half full. The time to fill the rest is (hours)
questions.explanation: Half the tank takes half the time: 4.

questions.question: An inlet fills a tank in 10 hours and an outlet empties it in 15 hours. With both open it fills in (hours)
A tank holds 240 litres. A tap delivers 20 litres per minute. It fills in (minutes)
A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. After 3 hours a leak that empties a full tank in 30 hours appears. The total time to fill the tank is (hours)
questions.explanation: Half the tank in 3 h. The rest at 2/15 per hour takes 3.75 h. Total 6.75.

questions.question: A tank is filled by a pipe in 4 hours but takes 5 hours because of a leak. The leak empties the full tank in (hours)
Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and a leak empties it in 20 hours. Both are open. The tank fills in (hours)
Two pipes fill a tank in 10 and 15 hours, and a leak empties it in 30 hours. With all three, the tank fills in (hours)
A tank that is half full is emptied by a leak that empties a full tank in 30 hours. The time to empty is (hours)
questions.explanation: Emptying half a tank takes half of 30 hours: 15 hours.

questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another in 8 hours. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, starting with the first. The tank fills in how many hours? (nearest 0.01)
questions.explanation: Three cycles (6 h) fill 21/24. 3/24 remains and the first pipe (4/24 per hour) takes 0.75 h: 6.75 hours.

questions.question: A cistern has a tap that fills it in 4 hours and a leak that empties it in 12 hours. After 2 hours the leak is repaired. The total time to fill the cistern is (hours)
questions.explanation: In 2 hours the net rate 1/6 fills 1/3. The remaining 2/3 at 1/4 per hour takes 8/3 hours. Total = 2 + 2.67 = 4.67.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 hours and pipe B empties it in 30 hours. A is opened for 10 hours alone, then B is also opened. Time to fill the rest after B opens is (hours)
questions.explanation: A fills half in 10 h. Net rate 1/60. The other half takes 30 hours.

questions.question: A tank can be filled in 9 hours by pipe A and emptied in 12 hours by pipe B. Starting empty, both are opened. The time to fill the tank is (hours)
A tap fills a tank in 5 hours. After 1 hour a leak develops that would empty a full tank in 20 hours. The total time to fill the tank is (hours)
questions.explanation: 1 hour fills 1/5. The net rate is 3/20, so 4/5 takes (4/5) ÷ (3/20) = 16/3 h. Total = 1 + 5.33 = 6.33.

questions.question: Three pipes fill a tank in 6, 8 and 12 hours. They work in turn for 1 hour each, starting with the 6-hour pipe. The time to fill the tank (nearest 0.1 hour) is (hours)
questions.explanation: A cycle fills 9/24. Two cycles (6 h) fill 18/24 and the 7th hour adds 4/24, giving 22/24. The 8-hour pipe needs 2/24 ÷ 3/24 = 0.67 h more: 7.67 ≈ 7.7 hours.

questions.question: A tap fills a bathtub at 15 litres per minute and the drain empties it at 5 litres per minute. A 200-litre tub takes (minutes)
A leak empties a full tank in 24 hours. A tap alone fills it in 8 hours. With the leak, the tank fills in (hours)
Two taps fill a tank in 12 and 16 hours. A third tap empties it in 24 hours. If all three are open, a half-full tank is filled in (hours)
